chunks: And from him, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said:

When it is the seventh day, and a boy or a girl has been born to one of you, let him perform Aqeeqa for him: a ram for the male, and similarly for the female. Perform Aqeeqa for him, feed the midwife from the Aqeeqa, and name him on the seventh day.

key_terms.عَقِيقَة: Aqeeqa: the ritual sacrifice of an animal for a newborn child

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for performing Aqeeqa for a newborn on the seventh day?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the Sunnah of Aqeeqa, emphasizing the seventh day as the optimal time for sacrifice, head shaving, and naming, thereby integrating gratitude with the child's formal entry into the community. It highlights the practical social dimension of the ritual by mandating that the midwife be fed from the sacrifice, reflecting the Shia emphasis on honoring those who facilitate the birth. The specification of gender-matching animals (ram for boy, ewe for girl) underscores the precision in following the Prophet's tradition as preserved in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
And from him, from a man, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>

having said: ‘When it is the seventh day, and a boy has been born to one of you, or a girl, so let him perform Aqeeqa for him, a ram for a male, and an ewe for a female, similar to that from it, and feed the midwife from the Aqeeqa, and name him on the seventh day’.
en.sarwar: 4. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from a man from abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, who has said the following:

“When it is the seventh day of childbirth in your home, a boy or a girl you must offer an Aqiqah in the form of slaughtering a ram for a boy and an ewe for a girl. When you offer an Aqiqah for him, feed al-Qabilah (the special nurse, doctor) thereof. You can give the child a name on the seventh day.’”
